task: Execute pre-revival infrastructure batch before RedCap revival scanning
user_intent: Norven approved executing items 1-3 together before starting the 360 old-RedCap scan: solidify the current develop baseline, fix Prism dispatcher timeout behavior, and build a formal Prism long-task sharding foundation that is more complete than a bare MVP.
main_claim: The batch is appropriate as a pre-revival infrastructure step if it remains bounded to runtime hardening, repository baseline stabilization, and a practical shard-account mechanism that the later 360 scan can immediately use.
changed_reality: No new code has been changed for this batch yet.
The worktree already contains uncommitted infrastructure changes from earlier approved hardening work; item 1 must review, commit, and push those before new revival migration work begins.
A prior Kimi provider dispatch did not return within the expected practical window and had to be manually cleaned up, so timeout behavior needs behavior-level proof.
Existing archaeology shard contracts mention long-task-context-defense, but there is not yet a formal Prism long-task sharding runtime account/check mechanism.
proposal: First review and commit/push the current infrastructure baseline to develop without mixing it with later old-RedCap migration changes.
Then harden prism-dispatch timeout handling with deterministic self-checks and visible expired-session recording.

Then add a Prism shard account foundation with bounded source scopes, provider/session binding, per-shard output schema, max rounds, Cap arbitration, merge/acceptance checks, and ledger/health integration.
Defer the 360 old-RedCap scan contract until these three items pass checks.
non_goals: Do not start broad old-RedCap scanning in this batch.
Do not add providers beyond Kimi and Claude Code.
Do not claim cross-host hook parity.
Do not build a full autonomous multi-agent scheduler beyond the foundation needed by the next scan phase.
review_questions: Is this 1-3 batch correctly bounded before 360 scanning?
What must the Prism long-task sharding foundation include so it is not an underpowered MVP?
What risks would make commit/push or dispatcher timeout work unsafe in the same batch?
What verification should be required before Cap reports this batch as ready for the 360 scan contract?
expected_output: Return strict JSON with provider, verdict, confidence, reality_delta, main_concern, top_risks, missing_evidence, minimum_fix, anti_loop_signal, and user_intent_alignment.
